   126	The following Proposition establishes that, for a fixed direction, a line
   127	$\line$ is an equivalence class of points on the line.
   128	\begin{proposition}
   129	  \label{prop:line-equiv}
   130	  Let $u,v \in \F_q^m$.
   131	  Then for all $u' \in \line(u,v)$, we have that $\line(u,v) = \line(u',v)$.
   132	\end{proposition}
   133	\begin{proof}
   134		Fix $u' \in \line(u,v)$.
   135	  We have that $u' = u + tv$ for some $t \in \F_q$.
   136	  Let $a \in \line(u,v)$.
   137	  This means that $a = u + sv$ for some $s\in \F_q$.
   138	  We also have that $a = u + (s - t + t)v = u + tv + (s - t)v = u' + (s - t)v$,
   139	  so $\line(u,v) \subseteq \line(u',v)$.
   140	  A similar argument shows that $\line(u',v) \subseteq \line(u,v)$.
   141	\end{proof}
   142	
   143	We now specify a canonical representation of lines $\line = \line(u,v)$ as pairs $(u_0,v)$
   144	where $u_0$ is a \emph{canonical representative} of $\line$ specified as
   145	follows.
   146	Let $L_v^{\lnf}: \F_q^m \to \F_q^m$ denote the canonical linear map with the
   147	one-dimensional kernel basis $\{v\}$ (see \Cref{def:cl-canonical} for a
   148	definition of canonical linear map).
   149	Note that for all $u \in \line$, we have that $L_v^{\lnf}(u)$ is a point in
   150	$\line$.
   151	This is because since the image and kernel of $L_v^{\lnf}$ are complementary
   152	subspaces by definition (see \Cref{def:cl-canonical}), any $u \in \F_q^m$ has a
   153	unique decomposition $u = u_0 + u_1$ where $u_0$ is in the image of $L_v^{\lnf}$
   154	and $u_1 \in \ker(L_v^{\lnf})$, which by definition is the subspace spanned by
   155	$v$.
   156	Thus $u_1 = tv$ for some $t \in \F_q$ and we have that $u_0 = u - tv \in \line$.
   157	In particular, if $u\in \line$ then $u_0 = L_v^{\lnf}(u) \in \line$ as well. 
   158	Furthermore, since $L_v^{\lnf}$ is a projection onto its image by definition, we
   159	have $L_v^{\lnf}(u_0) = u_0$.
   160	
   161	Next, note that for any $u,u' \in \line$, since $u-u' = sv$ for some $s\in \F_q$
   162	it follows that $L_v^\lnf(u) = L_v^\lnf(u')$.
   163	Thus $u_0 = u_0'$ and this shows that $L_v^\lnf$ gives a means to compute a
   164	canonical representative of lines.
   165	
   166	\begin{definition}[Canonical representative of a line]
   167	  \label{def:line-representative}
   168	  Let $\line$ be a line in direction $v$.
   169	  A canonical representative of $\line$ is the point $u_0 \in \F_q^m$ such that
   170	  \[
   171	    u_0 = L_v^\lnf(u)
   172	  \]
   173	  for all $u \in \line$.
   174	\end{definition}

   178	\paragraph{Question distribution.}
   179	We now present the question distribution of the game $\game^\ld$ as a typed CL
   180	distribution (see \Cref{sec:types} for the definition of typed CL functions and
   181	typed CL distributions).
   182	The type set $\type^\ld$ of the game $\game^\ld$ we use is
   183	\[
   184		\type^\ld = \{ \Point, \ALine, \DLine \}\;.
   185	\]
   186	The distribution over question types is uniform over $\type^\ld \times \type^\ld$. 
   187	
   188	We introduce the corresponding typed CL functions $L_\Point$, $L_\ALine$,
   189	$L_\DLine$ where the corresponding CL distributions $\mu_{L_\ALine,L_\Point}$
   190	and $\mu_{L_\DLine,L_\Point}$ implement the axis line-versus-point and diagonal
   191	line-versus-point distributions, respectively.
   192	The functions are parametrized by a field size $q$, a dimension $m$, and three
   193	complementary register subspaces $V_\xpt,V_{\coord}, V_{\dir{}}$ of some ambient
   194	space.
   195	The register $V_\xpt$ (which is isomorphic to $\F_q^m$) is called the
   196	\emph{point register}, $V_\coord$ (which is isomorphic to $\F_q$) is called the
   197	\emph{coordinate register}, and $V_{\dir{}}$ (which is isomorphic to $\F_q^m$)
   198	is called the \emph{direction register}, respectively.
   199	We let $V$ denote the direct sum $V_\xpt \oplus V_{\coord} \oplus V_{\dir{}}$.
   200	We identify elements of $V$ as triples $(u,s,v) \in \F_q^m \times \F_q \times
   201	\F_q^m$.
   202	
   203	Define $L_\Point$ to be the $1$-level CL function that projects onto $V_\xpt$: for every $(u,s,v) \in V$,
   204	\begin{equation}
   205	  \label{eq:cl-ptf}
   206		L_\Point(u,s,v) = (u,0,0) \;.
   207	\end{equation}
   208	Define $L_\ALine$ to be the following $2$-level CL function:
   209	\begin{equation}
   210	  \label{eq:cl-alnf}
   211		L_\ALine(u,s,v) = (L^\lnf_{e_i}(u), s, 0)\ \text{for all } (u,s,v) \in V,
   212	\end{equation}
   213	where $L^\lnf$ is the linear function used to compute the canonical
   214	representative of lines (see \Cref{def:line-representative}), and $i = \chi(s)$
   215	where we define $\chi(s)$ to be the unique integer such that
   216	\begin{equation}
   217	\label{eq:chi-func}
   218		s = (\chi(s) - 1) \frac{q}{m} + r
   219	\end{equation}
   220	for some $0 \leq r < q/m$, and we interpret the field element $s \in \F_q$ as an
   221	integer between $0$ and $q - 1$).
   222	The function $L_\ALine$ is the concatenation of the $1$-level CL function that
   223	projects the subspaces $V_{\coord} \oplus V_{\dir{}}$ down to $V_\coord$ (i.e.
   224	zeroes out the entire $V_{\dir{}}$ register), and the family of $1$-level CL
   225	functions $\{L^\lnf_{e_i} \}$ acting on $V_\xpt$, indexed by $i \in
   226	\{1,2,\ldots,m\}$.
   227	(See \Cref{lem:cl-concat} for definition of CL function concatenation.)
   228	Thus $L_\ALine$ is a $2$-level CL function.
   229	
   230	Define $L_\DLine$ to be the following $3$-level CL function: for all $(u,s,v) \in
   231	V$,
   232	\begin{equation}
   233	\label{eq:cl-dlnf}
   234		L_\DLine(u,s,v) = (L^\lnf_{\pi_{i-1}(v)}(u),s,\pi_{i-1}(v))
   235	\end{equation}
   236	where $i = \chi(s)$.
   237	The function $L_\DLine$ is the concatenation of the following CL functions (again, see \Cref{lem:cl-concat} for definition of CL function concatenation): (i) the identity function on $V_{\coord}$ (which is a $1$-level CL function); (ii) for every $i \in \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$ the $1$-level CL function on $V_{\dir{}}$ that maps $v \mapsto \pi_{i-1}(v)$ (i.e.~it zeroes out the first $i-1$ coordinates of $v$), and (iii) for every pair $(s,v') \in V_\coord \oplus V_{\dir{}}$, the $1$-level CL function $L^\lnf_{v'}$ acting on $V_\xpt$. Thus $L_\DLine$ is a $3$-level CL function.

   240	The following two lemmas establish that the CL functions
   241	$L_\Point,L_\ALine,L_\DLine$ give rise to the axis-parallel line-versus-point and
   242	diagonal line-versus-point distributions.
   243	\begin{lemma}
   244		\label{lem:alnf}
   245		Consider the pair $(\line, u)$ sampled in the following way: first, sample the
   246	  tuple $((u_0,s,0),(u,0,0))$ from the CL distribution $\mu_{L_\ALine,L_\Point}$,
   247	  and let $\line = \line(u_0,e_i)$ where $i = \chi(s)$.
   248	  Then $u$ is a uniformly random point in $\F_q^m$ and $\line$ is a line that
   249	  goes through $u$ and is parallel to a uniformly random axis $i \in
   250	  \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$.
   251	\end{lemma}
   252	\begin{proof}
   253		Since $s$ is uniformly random in $\F_q$ and $m$ divides $q$ by assumption, we
   254	  have that $i$ is uniformly random between $\{1,2,\ldots,m\}$ and therefore
   255	  $(u_0,s)$ specifies a uniformly random axis-parallel line $\line(u_0,e_i)$.
   256	  Since $u_0 = L^{\lnf}_{e_i}(u)$, we have that $u \in \line(u_0,e_i)$.
   257	\end{proof}

   394	We define a special class of measurements that are relevant to the soundness
   395	properties of the low-degree test.
   396	
   397	\begin{definition}[Low-degree polynomial measurements]
   398	  \label{def:ld-meas}
   399	  Define $\polymeas{m}{d}{q}$ to be the set of POVM measurements whose outcomes
   400	  correspond to (individual) degree-$d$ polynomials of $m$ variables over
   401	  $\F_q$.
   402	  More generally, for an integer $\ldc$ and tuples $m=(m_1, m_2, \ldots,
   403	  m_\ldc)$, $d=(d_1, d_2, \ldots, d_\ldc)$ and $q=(q_1, q_2, \ldots, q_\ldc)$,
   404	  we let $\simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ldc}$ be the set of measurements $G =
   405	  \{G_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots\,,\, g_\ldc}\}$ such that for $i\in\{1, 2, \ldots,
   406	  \ldc\}$, $g_i$ is a polynomial $g_i:\F_{q_i}^{m_i} \rightarrow
   407	  \F_{q_i}$ with individual degree $d_i$ (see \Cref{sec:ld-encoding} for a definition of individual degree). 
   408	\end{definition}

   410	Quantum soundness of a version of the classical low-degree test for polynomials of low \emph{total} degree was claimed
   411	in~\cite{natarajan2018low}, building on an analysis of a three-prover version of the test in~\cite{vidick2016three}. Unfortunately there is a gap in the soundness analysis of this test. For our construction we use the low individual degree test, whose quantum soundness is shown in~\cite{ML20} and generalized in~\cite{ji2021quantum}. We state the result in the form that is most directly useful for us, and show how the stated result follows from~\cite{ji2021quantum}.
   412	
   413	\begin{theorem}[Quantum soundness of the simultaneous classical low-degree test]
   414	  \label{lem:ld-soundness}
   415	  There exists a function $\delta_{\ld}(\eps, q, m, d, \ldc) = a (dm \ldc)^a (\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$ for universal constants $a\geq 1$ and $0<b\leq 1$ 
   416	such that the following
   417	  holds.
   418	  For all $\eps > 0$ and parameter tuple $\ldparams = (q, m, d, \ldc)$, for all
   419	  projective strategies $(\psi,A,B)$ that succeed with probability at least
   420	  $1-\eps$ in the game $\game^\ld_\ldparams$, there exists measurements
   421	  \[G^w \in \simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ldc}\] on $\mH_w$, for
   422	  $w\in\{\alice,\bob\}$, such that
   423	  \begin{equation*}
   424	    \begin{split}
   425	      A^{\Point,\, u}_{a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots\,,\, a_\ldc}
   426	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   427	      G^\bob_{[(g_1(u),g_2(u),\ldots,g_\ldc(u)) = (a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots \,,\, a_\ldc)]}\;,\\
   428	      G^\alice_{[(g_1(u),g_2(u),\ldots,g_\ldc(u)) = (a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots \,,\, a_\ldc)]}
   429	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   430				 B^{\Point,\, u}_{a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots\,,\, a_\ldc}\;,\\
   431	      G^\alice_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots \,,\, g_\ldc}
   432	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   433	      G^\bob_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots \,,\, g_\ldc}\;,
   434	    \end{split}
   435	  \end{equation*}
   436	  where $\delta_{\ld} = \delta_{\ld}(\eps, q, m, d, \ldc)$, 
   437	  and all three statements are with respect to the state $\ket{\psi}$.
   438	In addition, the first two approximations hold under the uniform distribution over $u\in \F_q^m$,
   439		whereas there is no question distribution associated with the third approximation.
   440	\end{theorem}

   442	\begin{proof}
   443	Let $\ldparams = (q, m, d, \ldc)$
   444	where $m, d, \ldc \in \N$ are integers, $q \in \N$ is an admissible field size,
   445	and $m$ divides $q$. Let $\Sigma=\F_q$. Let $\code \subseteq \Sigma^q$ be the Reed-Solomon code with degree $d$. Explicitly, $\code$ is the set of all $(p(x_1),\ldots,p(x_n))$ where $p:\F_q\to\F_q$ is a univariate polynomial of degree at most $d$ and $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ are an enumeration of $\F_q$. Then in the (standard) notation from~\cite{ji2021quantum} $\code$ is a linear $[q,d+1,n-d+1]_\Sigma$ code.
   446	
   447	Observe that the two-prover tensor code test, for the code $\code^{\otimes m}$, as described in~\cite[Figure 1 and Figure 2]{ji2021quantum}, is identical to the game $\game^\ld$ with parameters $\ldparams$ and $\ldc=1$, whose decider is presented in Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider}. This is because 
   448	\begin{enumerate}
   449	\item The \emph{axis-parallel line-versus-point test} from Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} is identical to the \emph{axis-parallel lines test} from~\cite[Figure 1]{ji2021quantum}, with the only difference that in Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} the roles of A and B are chosen uniformly at random. This is consistent with the two-prover variant of the tensor code test from~\cite[Section 4.1]{ji2021quantum}.
   450	\item The \emph{diagonal line-versus-point test} from Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} is identical to the \emph{subcube commutation test} from~\cite[Figure 1]{ji2021quantum}, with again the added symmetrization between players. 
   451	\item The \emph{consistency test} from Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} is identical to the \emph{synchronicity test} from~\cite[Figure 2]{ji2021quantum}.
   452	\end{enumerate}
   453	
   454	As a result,~\cite[Theorem 4.7]{ji2021quantum}, in which we choose the parameter $k$ as $k=m^3d$,  immediately yields \Cref{lem:ld-soundness}.
   455	
   456	To conclude it remains to extend the result to the case of general $\ldc$. This is done 
   457	via a standard reduction, following exactly the same steps as the derivation of Theorem 4.43 from Theorem 4.40 in~\cite{NW19}.
   458	\end{proof}

   465	\subsubsection{Complexity of the classical low-degree test.}
   466	The CL functions and decision procedure of the low-degree test are incorporated
   467	as subroutines in some of the normal form verifiers constructed in subsequent

   472	the decision procedure $\decider^\ld$ as a Turing machine, given the parameter
   473	tuple $\ldparams$ as input.

   477	\begin{lemma}[Complexity of the classical low-degree test]
   478	  \label{lem:ld-complexity}

   612	The following theorem records the self-testing (also known as \emph{rigidity})
   613	properties of the Magic Square game.
   614	Its self-testing properties
   615	are crucial to the Pauli basis test.
   616	In particular, it is used to enforce anticommutation relations between certain
   617	pairs of operators.
   618	We will refer to this theorem in the proof of the soundness of the Pauli basis test (\Cref{thm:pauli} below) in \Cref{sec:qld-analysis}.
   619	
   620	\begin{theorem}[Rigidity of the Magic Square game]
   621	  \label{thm:ms-rigidity}
   622	
   623	
   624	Let $\strategy = (\ket{\psi},A,B)$ be a strategy that succeeds in the Magic Square game $\game^{\MS}$ with probability $1 - \eps$, where $\ket{\psi} \in \mH_A \otimes \mH_B$ is a state. Then there exist local isometries $\phi_A: \mH_A \to \mH_{A'} \otimes \mH_{A''},\phi_B: \mH_B \to \mH_{B'} \otimes \mH_{B''}$ (where $\mH_{A'},\mH_{B'} \cong (\C^2)^{\otimes 2}$ and $\mH_{A''},\mH_{B''}$ are finite dimensional) and a state $\ket{\aux} \in \mH_{A''} \otimes \mH_{B''}$ such that 
   625	\begin{enumerate}
   626	    \item $\left \| \phi_A \otimes \phi_B \ket{\psi} - \ket{\EPR_2}^{\otimes 2} \otimes \ket{\aux} \right \| \leq O(\sqrt{\eps})$,
   627	    \item Letting $\tilde{A}^x_a = \phi_A\, A^x_a \, \phi_A^\dagger$ and $\tilde{B}^y_b = \phi_B B^y_b \phi_B^\dagger$, we have that
   628	    \begin{gather*}
   629	        \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1}_b \otimes I_{B'B''} \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} (\sigma^X_b)_{A'} \otimes I_{A'' B' B''} \\
   630	        \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5}_b \otimes I_{B'B''} \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} (\sigma^Z_b)_{A'} \otimes I_{A'' B' B''} \\
   631	        I_{A'A''} \otimes \tilde{B}^{\Variable_1}_b    \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} I_{A' A'' B''} \otimes (\sigma^X_b)_{B'} \\
   632	        I_{A'A''} \otimes \tilde{B}^{\Variable_5}_b    \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} I_{A' A'' B''} \otimes (\sigma^Z_b)_{B'}
   633	    \end{gather*}
   634	    where the $\approx_{\sqrt{\eps}}$ statement holds with respect to the state $\ket{\EPR_2}^{\otimes 2}_{A'B'} \otimes \ket{\aux}_{A''B''}$ and the answer summation is over $b \in \{0,1\}$. As a consequence, letting 
   635	    \begin{gather*}
   636	    \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1} = \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1}_0 - \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1}_1 \\
   637	    \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5} = \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5}_0 - \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5}_1 \\
   638	    \end{gather*}
   639	    it holds that
   640	    \begin{gather*}
   641	        \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1} \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5} \otimes I_{B' B''} \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} - \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5}  \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1} \otimes I_{B' B''} \\
   642	        I_{A' A''} \otimes \tilde{B}^{\Variable_1} \tilde{B}^{\Variable_5}  \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} - I_{A' A''} \otimes \tilde{B}^{\Variable_5}  \tilde{B}^{\Variable_1} \;,
   643	      \end{gather*}
   644	      where the notation $M \approx_{\delta} N$ for $M, N$ that are not POVM
   645	      elements means
   646	      \[  \bra{\psi} (M-N)^\dagger (M-N) \ket{\psi}  \leq  O(\delta). \]
   647	\end{enumerate}
   648	
   649	\end{theorem}
   650	\begin{proof}
   651	 	A proof of the rigidity of the Magic Square game can be found in~\cite[Theorem 6.9]{coladangelo2017robust}. There are a couple minor differences between their rigidity statement and the one stated here. First, they state that the robustness of the Magic Square self-test is $O(\eps)$; however they specify the closeness between the actual and ideal states in terms of the trace norm, whereas we specify the closeness between $\phi_\alice \otimes \phi_\bob \ket{\psi}$ and $\ket{\EPR_2}^{\otimes 2}\otimes \ket{\aux}$ in terms of the Euclidean distance, which translates to $O(\sqrt{\eps})$ instead of $O(\eps)$. Second, their choice of ideal strategy specifies that the observables corresponding to $\Variable_1$ and $\Variable_5$ questions are $I \otimes \sigma^Z$ and $\sigma^{Z} \sigma^{X} \otimes \sigma^Z \sigma^X$; however under a local change of basis these are equivalent to $\sigma^X \otimes I$ and $\sigma^Z \otimes I$ respectively.
   652	\end{proof}

  1449	
  1450	The strategies described in the proof of \Cref{lem:pauli-completeness} and in the conclusion of \Cref{thm:pauli} are described in terms of qudit Pauli measurements and maximally entangled states defined over $q$-dimensional qudits. 
  1451	However, it is more convenient for our application of the Pauli basis test to
  1452	instead deal with \emph{qubits}.
  1453	In particular, we use the Pauli basis test in the ``introspection game'' of
  1454	Section~\ref{sec:introspection}, where the players are commanded to sample
  1455	questions according to a sampler $\sampler$ of a normal form verifier.
  1456	By definition of normal form verifier, $\sampler$ is a sampler over $\F_2$, and
  1457	therefore it is natural to use a test for qubit Pauli measurements.
  1458	
  1459	Since we use field sizes $q$ that are powers of $2$, Lemma~\ref{lem:pauli-binary}
  1460	shows that the conclusions of \Cref{thm:pauli} can also be described in terms of
  1461	testing for maximally entangled states over qubits and qubit Pauli measurements.

  1483	    	\bigotimes_{i=1}^{M} \bigotimes_{j=1}^{\log q} \sigma^W_{u_{ij}}

  1492	\subsubsection{Canonical parameters and complexity of the Pauli basis test}
  1493	\label{sec:qld-complexity}
  1494	
  1495	We specify a canonical setting of the parameter tuple $\qldparams$ as a function
  1496	of an integer $R$.
  1497	We call this canonical setting $\introparams$ because we use these in the
  1498	``introspection'' section (\Cref{sec:introspection}).
  1499	We then give bounds on the complexity of computing the decision procedure and CL
  1500	functions of the Pauli basis test corresponding to the parameter tuple
  1501	$\qldparams$, as a function of $R$.
  1502	
  1503	\begin{definition}[Canonical parameters of the Pauli basis test]
  1504	  \label{def:introparams}
  1505	  Let $a,b$ be the universal constants specified in Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli}.
  1506	  Let $c$ denote the smallest even integer that is at least $(b + a)/b$.
  1507	  For all integers $R \geq 4$, define the tuple $\introparams(R) = (q,m,d)$
  1508	  where
  1509	  \begin{itemize}
  1510	  	\item $q = 2^k$ for $k = c \lceil  \log \log R  \rceil + 1$.
  1511		\item $m = 2^j$ where $2^j \leq c \lceil \log R \rceil + 1 < 2^{j+1}$. 
  1512		\item $d = 1$. 
  1513	  \end{itemize}
  1514	\end{definition}
  1515	
  1516	Intuitively, this choice of parameters is such that the Pauli basis test
  1517	certifies the presence of an $M=2^m$-qudit EPR state (of local dimension $q$), or
  1518	equivalently an $M\log q$-qubit EPR state.
  1519	
  1520	\begin{lemma}
  1521	  \label{lem:delta-bound}
  1522	 For all integers $R \geq 4$, the parameter tuple $\introparams(R) = (q,m,d)$ is
  1523	  admissible (see Definition~\ref{def:admissible}), satisfies $2^m \geq R$, and furthermore there exist
  1524	  universal constants $a'\geq 1$ and $0 < b' \leq 1$ such that the function
  1525	  $\delta_\qld(\eps, m, d, q)$ from Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli} is at most
  1526	   \[
  1527	   	a' ( \log(R)^{a'} \cdot \eps^{b'} + \log(R)^{-b'}) \;.
  1528		\]
  1529	\end{lemma}
  1530	
  1531	\begin{proof}
  1532	  We verify the admissibility of $\introparams(R)$ first: the field size $q =
  1533	  2^k$ is admissible because $k$ is odd. We have $m | q$ because for all $R \geq 4$ we have  
  1534	  \[
  1535	  	2^j \leq 2 c \lceil \log R \rceil \leq 2 \log^c R \leq 2^k~.
  1536	  \]
  1537		Next, we show that $R \leq 2^m$. Since $m = 2^j \geq (c/2) \log R$, we have that
  1538		\[
  1539			2^m \geq R^{c/2} \geq R
  1540		\]
  1541		where we used that $c \geq 2$. 
  1542	
  1543	Finally, we show the desired bound on the error function $\delta_\qld(\eps,m,d,q)$. First, observe that $2^{-bmd} \leq q^{-b}$ because $k \leq m$.
  1544	  Note that for $R \geq 2$, we have $m \leq 2c \log R$, and furthermore $q =
  1545	  2^k \geq \log^c R$.
  1546	Then, we get
  1547	\begin{align*}
  1548	  	\delta_\qld(\eps,m,d,q)
  1549	    & = a (md)^a (\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd}) \tag{by Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli}}  \\
  1550	    & \leq a (md)^a (\eps^b + 2q^{-b}) \tag{because  $2^{-bmd} \leq q^{-b}$}  \\
  1551	    & = a (m)^a (\eps^b + 2q^{-b}) \tag{because  $d=1$}  \\
  1552	    & \leq a (2c)^a \log^{a} (R) ( \eps^{b} + 2q^{-b}) \tag{because  $m \leq 2c \log R$}\\
  1553	    & \leq a (2c)^a \log^{a} (R) ( \eps^{b} + 2(\log R)^{-cb}) \tag{because  $q \geq \log^c R$}\\
  1554	    & \leq 2a (2c)^a \log^{a} (R) ( \eps^{b} + (\log R)^{-cb}) \\
  1555	    & = 2a (2c)^a ( (\log R)^{a}\eps^{b} + (\log R)^{a-cb}) \\
  1556	    & \leq 2a(2c)^{a} \left ( (\log R)^{a} \eps^{b}
  1557	      + (\log R)^{-b} \right) \tag{because  $cb - a \geq b \geq 0$}\\
  1558	    & \leq a' ( (\log R)^{a'} \eps^{b} + (\log R)^{-b}),
  1559	  \end{align*}
  1560	  where $a'$ is defined as the quantity $2a(2c)^a$.
  1561	This completes the proof of the lemma.
  1562	\end{proof}
  1563	
  1564	\begin{lemma}
  1565		\label{lem:introparams-complexity}
  1566		Fix an integer $R \geq 4$, let $\introparams(R) = (q,m,d)$.
  1567		The integers $(q,m,d) = \introparams(R)$ can be computed in time $\polylog
  1568	  R$ when given the binary representation of $R$ as input.
  1569	\end{lemma}
  1570	\begin{proof}

    27	
    28	/-- The bit register obtained by expanding every Pauli-register field element
    29	in the basis stored by `P.model`. -/
    30	abbrev QubitRegister (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
    31	  Cube P.m × Fin P.model.basisDim → ZMod 2

    33	/-- The ideal auxiliary state tensored with the qubit EPR register, in the
    34	local-player ordering used by `cor:pauli-binary`. -/
    35	noncomputable def idealQubitState (P : AdmissibleParams)
    36	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    37	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
    38	    (aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × ιB')) :
    39	    EuclideanSpace ℂ
    40	      ((ιA' × QubitRegister P) × (ιB' × QubitRegister P)) :=
    41	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv
    42	      ((ιA' × QubitRegister P) × (ιB' × QubitRegister P)) ℂ).symm
    43	    (fun p =>
    44	      (EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιA' × ιB') ℂ aux (p.1.1, p.2.1)) *
    45	        (EuclideanSpace.equiv (QubitRegister P × QubitRegister P) ℂ
    46	          (eprState (QubitRegister P)) (p.1.2, p.2.2)))

    49	`cor:pauli-binary`; this structure introduces no hypothesis beyond the paper
    50	theorem. -/
    51	structure QubitSoundnessWitness (P : AdmissibleParams)
    52	    (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P)) where
    53	  ιA' : Type
    54	  ιB' : Type
    55	  [ιAFintype : Fintype ιA']
    56	  [ιBFintype : Fintype ιB']
    57	  [ιADecidableEq : DecidableEq ιA']
    58	  [ιBDecidableEq : DecidableEq ιB']
    59	  φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
    60	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × QubitRegister P)
    61	  φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
    62	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × QubitRegister P)
    63	  aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × ιB')
    64	  aux_norm : ‖aux‖ = 1

    67	  QubitSoundnessWitness.ιBFintype QubitSoundnessWitness.ιADecidableEq
    68	  QubitSoundnessWitness.ιBDecidableEq
    69	
    70	/-- Alice's ideal qubit projector placed on the joint target space. -/
    71	noncomputable def qubitProjOnA'' (P : AdmissibleParams)
    72	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    73	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB'] (W : PauliKind)
    74	    (u : PauliRegister P) :
    75	    Op ((ιA' × QubitRegister P) × (ιB' × QubitRegister P)) :=

    92	/-- Lift a conjugated Alice effect to the full qubit target space. -/
    93	noncomputable def liftedQubitAEffect {P : AdmissibleParams} {G : Game}
    94	    (S : Strategy G) {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    95	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
    96	    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ]

    98	    (M : Op S.ιA) :
    99	    Op ((ιA' × QubitRegister P) × (ιB' × QubitRegister P)) :=

   102	/-- Lift a conjugated Bob effect to the full qubit target space. -/
   103	noncomputable def liftedQubitBEffect {P : AdmissibleParams} {G : Game}
   104	    (S : Strategy G) {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   105	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
   106	    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ]

   108	    (M : Op S.ιB) :

   112	/-- Alice's qubit-projector family distance in `cor:pauli-binary`. -/
   113	noncomputable def qubitOperatorDistanceA
   114	    (P : AdmissibleParams) (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P))
   115	    (w : QubitSoundnessWitness P S) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
   116	  ∑ u : PauliRegister P,
   117	    ‖applyOperatorToState
   118	      (liftedQubitAEffect S w.φA
   119	          ((S.A (pauliQuestion P W)).effect (.pauliOutcome u)) -
   120	        qubitProjOnA'' P W u)

   123	/-- Bob's qubit-projector family distance in `cor:pauli-binary`. -/
   124	noncomputable def qubitOperatorDistanceB
   125	    (P : AdmissibleParams) (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P))
   126	    (w : QubitSoundnessWitness P S) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
   127	  ∑ u : PauliRegister P,
   128	    ‖applyOperatorToState
   129	      (liftedQubitBEffect S w.φB
   130	          ((S.B (pauliQuestion P W)).effect (.pauliOutcome u)) -
   131	        qubitProjOnB'' P W u)
   132	      (idealQubitState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2

   135	coordinates. Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:430-454`, paper
   136	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1450-1491`.
   137	
   138	The theorem retains the source-compatible nonnegative error boundary and uses
   139	only `P.model` and its stored basis dimension. -/
   140	theorem pauli_soundness_qubit :
   141	    ∃ a b : ℝ, 1 ≤ a ∧ 0 < b ∧ b < 1 ∧
   142	      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ), 0 ≤ ε →
   143	        ∀ S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P), 1 - ε ≤ S.value →
   144	          ∃ w : QubitSoundnessWitness P S,
   145	            ‖isometryTensor w.φA w.φB S.ψ - idealQubitState P w.aux‖ ≤
   146	                deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q ∧
   147	            (∀ W : PauliKind,
   148	              qubitOperatorDistanceA P S w W ≤
   149	                deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q) ∧
   150	            ∀ W : PauliKind,
   151	              qubitOperatorDistanceB P S w W ≤
   152	                deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q := by
   153	  sorry
   154	
   155	end

     4	/-!
     5	# Pauli basis test soundness
     6	
     7	The quantitative error function and the source-shaped soundness statement live
     8	here.  All analytic estimates are intentionally proof-level obligations in the
     9	stage-4.1 skeleton; the carriers below are concrete finite-dimensional vectors
    10	and matrices so that later proofs can use the existing Hilbert-space API.
    11	
    12	## References
    13	
    14	The main declaration is `thm:pauli` in
    15	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:407-424`, with paper origin
    16	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
    17	The distance functionals use `def:state-distance` and `def:povm-distance` from
    18	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:187-226`.
    19	-/
    20	
    21	open scoped BigOperators Matrix ComplexOrder
    22	
    23	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    24	
    25	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    26	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    27	
    28	noncomputable section
    29	
    30	/-- The Pauli-test error scale.  The argument order is `(a, b, ε, m, d, q)`;
    31	the powers are real `rpow`s and the asymptotic constants are absorbed into `a`,
    32	as specified by `thm:pauli` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:407-424`,
    33	paper `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`).
    34	-/
    35	noncomputable def deltaQld (a b ε : ℝ) (m d q : ℕ) : ℝ :=
    36	  a * Real.rpow ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) a *
    37	    (Real.rpow ε b + Real.rpow (q : ℝ) (-b) +
    38	      Real.rpow 2 (-(b * ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ))))
    39	
    40	/-- The ideal auxiliary state `aux ⊗ EPR_q^{⊗M}` in the shuffled register
    41	ordering.  The EPR factor is the concrete `eprState` from
    42	`def:EPR` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:537-547`; paper
    43	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:946-955`).
    44	-/
    45	noncomputable def idealState (P : AdmissibleParams)
    46	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    47	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
    48	    (aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × ιB')) :
    49	    EuclideanSpace ℂ ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
    50	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) ×
    51	      (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) ℂ).symm
    52	    (fun p =>
    53	      ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιA' × ιB') ℂ) aux (p.1.1, p.2.1)) *
    54	        ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P) ℂ)
    55	          (eprState (PauliRegister P)) (p.1.2, p.2.2)))
    56	
    57	/-- The Pauli question carrying no additional coefficient data, as in
    58	`def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:350-386`, paper origin
    59	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1006-1008`.
    60	-/
    61	def pauliQuestion (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind) : PauliQuestion P :=
    62	  (.pauli W, 0)
    63	
    64	/-- The A-side ideal Pauli projector, with identities on the auxiliary and
    65	B-side registers.  This is a concrete matrix form of the operator comparison
    66	in `thm:pauli` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:407-424`; paper
    67	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`).
    68	-/
    69	noncomputable def pauliProjOnA'' (P : AdmissibleParams)
    70	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    71	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB'] (W : PauliKind)
    72	    (u : PauliRegister P) :
    73	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
    74	  fun p q =>
    75	    if p.1.1 = q.1.1 ∧ p.2 = q.2 then
    76	      pauliProj W u p.1.2 q.1.2
    77	    else 0
    78	
    79	/-- The symmetric B-side ideal Pauli projector from `thm:pauli`, blueprint
    80	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:407-424`, paper origin
    81	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
    82	-/
    83	noncomputable def pauliProjOnB'' (P : AdmissibleParams)
    84	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    85	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB'] (W : PauliKind)
    86	    (u : PauliRegister P) :
    87	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
    88	  fun p q =>
    89	    if p.1 = q.1 ∧ p.2.1 = q.2.1 then
    90	      pauliProj W u p.2.2 q.2.2
    91	    else 0
    92	
    93	/-- Lift a conjugated A-side effect to the full ideal register in `thm:pauli`,
    94	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:407-424`, paper origin
    95	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
    96	-/
    97	noncomputable def liftedAEffect {P : AdmissibleParams} {G : Game}
    98	    (S : Strategy G) {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    99	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
   100	    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   101	      EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × PauliRegister P))
   102	    (M : Op S.ιA) :
   103	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
   104	  fun p q =>
   105	    if p.2 = q.2 then
   106	      (conjIsometry φA M) p.1 q.1
   107	    else 0
   108	
   109	/-- Lift a conjugated B-side effect to the full ideal register in `thm:pauli`,
   110	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:407-424`, paper origin
   111	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   112	-/
   113	noncomputable def liftedBEffect {P : AdmissibleParams} {G : Game}
   114	    (S : Strategy G) {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   115	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
   116	    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   117	      EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × PauliRegister P))
   118	    (M : Op S.ιB) :
   119	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
   120	  fun p q =>
   121	    if p.1 = q.1 then
   122	      (conjIsometry φB M) p.2 q.2
   123	    else 0
   124	
   125	/-- A finite witness packaging the auxiliary dimensions, isometries, and state
   126	from `thm:pauli`.  This structure is a Lean-only encoding of the existential
   127	data in the paper theorem; it introduces no extra hypothesis.  Blueprint
   128	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:407-424`, paper origin
   129	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   130	-/
   131	structure PauliSoundnessWitness (P : AdmissibleParams)
   132	    (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P)) where
   133	  ιA' : Type
   134	  ιB' : Type
   135	  [ιAFintype : Fintype ιA']
   136	  [ιBFintype : Fintype ιB']
   137	  [ιADecidableEq : DecidableEq ιA']
   138	  [ιBDecidableEq : DecidableEq ιB']
   139	  φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   140	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × PauliRegister P)
   141	  φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   142	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × PauliRegister P)
   143	  aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × ιB')
   144	  aux_norm : ‖aux‖ = 1
   145	
   146	attribute [instance] PauliSoundnessWitness.ιAFintype PauliSoundnessWitness.ιBFintype
   147	  PauliSoundnessWitness.ιADecidableEq PauliSoundnessWitness.ιBDecidableEq
   148	
   149	/-- The A-side operator-distance quantity appearing in the soundness
   150	conclusion.  It is the finite-sum realization of `def:povm-distance` from
   151	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:219-226`, paper origin
   152	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`.
   153	-/
   154	noncomputable def pauliOperatorDistanceA
   155	    (P : AdmissibleParams) (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P))
   156	    (w : PauliSoundnessWitness P S) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
   157	  ∑ u : PauliRegister P,
   158	      ‖applyOperatorToState (liftedAEffect S w.φA
   159	        ((S.A (pauliQuestion P W)).effect (.pauliOutcome u)) -
   160	      pauliProjOnA'' P W u) (idealState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2
   161	
   162	/-- The symmetric B-side operator-distance quantity from `def:povm-distance`,
   163	blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:219-226`, paper origin
   164	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`.
   165	-/
   166	noncomputable def pauliOperatorDistanceB
   167	    (P : AdmissibleParams) (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P))
   168	    (w : PauliSoundnessWitness P S) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
   169	  ∑ u : PauliRegister P,
   170	      ‖applyOperatorToState (liftedBEffect S w.φB
   171	        ((S.B (pauliQuestion P W)).effect (.pauliOutcome u)) -
   172	      pauliProjOnB'' P W u) (idealState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2
   173	
   174	/-- `thm:pauli`: every sufficiently successful Pauli basis test strategy admits
   175	local isometries and an auxiliary unit state for which the state and both
   176	operator families are close at scale `deltaQld`.  The theorem uses the
   177	once-and-for-all self-dual-normal field model selected by `fixedFieldModel` for
   178	each admissible size, rather than a freshly quantified field identification.
   179	Blueprint
   180	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:407-424`; paper origin
   181	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   182	
   183	The paper's asymptotic constants are encoded by the explicit `deltaQld`
   184	functional; the squared operator distances use the quantitative convention of
   185	`def:povm-distance` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:219-226`).
   186	-/
   187	theorem pauli_soundness :
   188	    ∃ a b : ℝ, 1 ≤ a ∧ 0 < b ∧ b < 1 ∧
   189	      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ), 0 ≤ ε →
   190	        ∀ S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P), 1 - ε ≤ S.value →
   191	          ∃ w : PauliSoundnessWitness P S,
   192	            ‖isometryTensor w.φA w.φB S.ψ - idealState P w.aux‖ ≤
   193	                deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q ∧
   194	            (∀ W : PauliKind,
   195	              pauliOperatorDistanceA P S w W ≤ deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q) ∧
   196	            (∀ W : PauliKind,
   197	              pauliOperatorDistanceB P S w W ≤ deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q) := by
   198	  sorry
   199	
   200	end
   201	
   202	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

   394	We define a special class of measurements that are relevant to the soundness
   395	properties of the low-degree test.
   396	
   397	\begin{definition}[Low-degree polynomial measurements]
   398	  \label{def:ld-meas}
   399	  Define $\polymeas{m}{d}{q}$ to be the set of POVM measurements whose outcomes
   400	  correspond to (individual) degree-$d$ polynomials of $m$ variables over
   401	  $\F_q$.
   402	  More generally, for an integer $\ldc$ and tuples $m=(m_1, m_2, \ldots,
   403	  m_\ldc)$, $d=(d_1, d_2, \ldots, d_\ldc)$ and $q=(q_1, q_2, \ldots, q_\ldc)$,
   404	  we let $\simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ldc}$ be the set of measurements $G =
   405	  \{G_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots\,,\, g_\ldc}\}$ such that for $i\in\{1, 2, \ldots,
   406	  \ldc\}$, $g_i$ is a polynomial $g_i:\F_{q_i}^{m_i} \rightarrow
   407	  \F_{q_i}$ with individual degree $d_i$ (see \Cref{sec:ld-encoding} for a definition of individual degree). 
   408	\end{definition}
   409	
   410	Quantum soundness of a version of the classical low-degree test for polynomials of low \emph{total} degree was claimed
   411	in~\cite{natarajan2018low}, building on an analysis of a three-prover version of the test in~\cite{vidick2016three}. Unfortunately there is a gap in the soundness analysis of this test. For our construction we use the low individual degree test, whose quantum soundness is shown in~\cite{ML20} and generalized in~\cite{ji2021quantum}. We state the result in the form that is most directly useful for us, and show how the stated result follows from~\cite{ji2021quantum}.
   412	
   413	\begin{theorem}[Quantum soundness of the simultaneous classical low-degree test]
   414	  \label{lem:ld-soundness}
   415	  There exists a function $\delta_{\ld}(\eps, q, m, d, \ldc) = a (dm \ldc)^a (\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$ for universal constants $a\geq 1$ and $0<b\leq 1$ 
   416	such that the following
   417	  holds.
   418	  For all $\eps > 0$ and parameter tuple $\ldparams = (q, m, d, \ldc)$, for all
   419	  projective strategies $(\psi,A,B)$ that succeed with probability at least
   420	  $1-\eps$ in the game $\game^\ld_\ldparams$, there exists measurements
   421	  \[G^w \in \simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ldc}\] on $\mH_w$, for
   422	  $w\in\{\alice,\bob\}$, such that
   423	  \begin{equation*}
   424	    \begin{split}
   425	      A^{\Point,\, u}_{a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots\,,\, a_\ldc}
   426	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   427	      G^\bob_{[(g_1(u),g_2(u),\ldots,g_\ldc(u)) = (a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots \,,\, a_\ldc)]}\;,\\
   428	      G^\alice_{[(g_1(u),g_2(u),\ldots,g_\ldc(u)) = (a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots \,,\, a_\ldc)]}
   429	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   430				 B^{\Point,\, u}_{a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots\,,\, a_\ldc}\;,\\
   431	      G^\alice_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots \,,\, g_\ldc}
   432	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   433	      G^\bob_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots \,,\, g_\ldc}\;,
   434	    \end{split}
   435	  \end{equation*}
   436	  where $\delta_{\ld} = \delta_{\ld}(\eps, q, m, d, \ldc)$, 
   437	  and all three statements are with respect to the state $\ket{\psi}$.
   438	In addition, the first two approximations hold under the uniform distribution over $u\in \F_q^m$,
   439		whereas there is no question distribution associated with the third approximation.
   440	\end{theorem}
   441	
   442	\begin{proof}
   443	Let $\ldparams = (q, m, d, \ldc)$
   444	where $m, d, \ldc \in \N$ are integers, $q \in \N$ is an admissible field size,
   445	and $m$ divides $q$. Let $\Sigma=\F_q$. Let $\code \subseteq \Sigma^q$ be the Reed-Solomon code with degree $d$. Explicitly, $\code$ is the set of all $(p(x_1),\ldots,p(x_n))$ where $p:\F_q\to\F_q$ is a univariate polynomial of degree at most $d$ and $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ are an enumeration of $\F_q$. Then in the (standard) notation from~\cite{ji2021quantum} $\code$ is a linear $[q,d+1,n-d+1]_\Sigma$ code.
   446	
   447	Observe that the two-prover tensor code test, for the code $\code^{\otimes m}$, as described in~\cite[Figure 1 and Figure 2]{ji2021quantum}, is identical to the game $\game^\ld$ with parameters $\ldparams$ and $\ldc=1$, whose decider is presented in Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider}. This is because 
   448	\begin{enumerate}
   449	\item The \emph{axis-parallel line-versus-point test} from Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} is identical to the \emph{axis-parallel lines test} from~\cite[Figure 1]{ji2021quantum}, with the only difference that in Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} the roles of A and B are chosen uniformly at random. This is consistent with the two-prover variant of the tensor code test from~\cite[Section 4.1]{ji2021quantum}.
   450	\item The \emph{diagonal line-versus-point test} from Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} is identical to the \emph{subcube commutation test} from~\cite[Figure 1]{ji2021quantum}, with again the added symmetrization between players. 
   451	\item The \emph{consistency test} from Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} is identical to the \emph{synchronicity test} from~\cite[Figure 2]{ji2021quantum}.
   452	\end{enumerate}
   453	
   454	As a result,~\cite[Theorem 4.7]{ji2021quantum}, in which we choose the parameter $k$ as $k=m^3d$,  immediately yields \Cref{lem:ld-soundness}.
   455	
   456	To conclude it remains to extend the result to the case of general $\ldc$. This is done 
   457	via a standard reduction, following exactly the same steps as the derivation of Theorem 4.43 from Theorem 4.40 in~\cite{NW19}.
   458	\end{proof}

   466	The CL functions and decision procedure of the low-degree test are incorporated
   467	as subroutines in some of the normal form verifiers constructed in subsequent
   468	sections.
   469	The next lemma establishes the time complexity of these procedures as a function

   472	the decision procedure $\decider^\ld$ as a Turing machine, given the parameter
   473	tuple $\ldparams$ as input.

   478	  \label{lem:ld-complexity}

   480	  \begin{enumerate}
   481		\item The time complexity of the decision procedure $\decider^\ld$
   482	    parametrized by $\ldparams$ is $\poly(m, d, k, \log q)$.
   483		\item The time complexity of evaluating marginals of the CL functions
   484	    $L_\Point$, $L_\ALine$, and $L_\DLine$ at a given input point is $\poly(m, \log
   485	    q)$.

   613	properties of the Magic Square game.
   614	Its self-testing properties
   615	are crucial to the Pauli basis test.
   616	In particular, it is used to enforce anticommutation relations between certain
   617	pairs of operators.

   620	\begin{theorem}[Rigidity of the Magic Square game]
   621	  \label{thm:ms-rigidity}
   622	
   623	
   624	Let $\strategy = (\ket{\psi},A,B)$ be a strategy that succeeds in the Magic Square game $\game^{\MS}$ with probability $1 - \eps$, where $\ket{\psi} \in \mH_A \otimes \mH_B$ is a state.    625	\begin{enumerate}
   626	    \item $\left \| \phi_A \otimes \phi_B \ket{\psi} - \ket{\EPR_2}^{\otimes 2} \otimes \ket{\aux} \right \| \leq O(\sqrt{\eps})$,
   627	    \item Letting $\tilde{A}^x_a = \phi_A\, A^x_a \, \phi_A^\dagger$ and $\tilde{B}^y_b = \phi_B B^y_b \phi_B^\dagger$, we have that
   628	    \begin{gather*}

   630	        \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5}_b \otimes I_{B'B''} \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} (\sigma^Z_b)_{A'} \otimes I_{A'' B' B''} \\

   635	    \begin{gather*}
   636	    \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1} = \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1}_0 - \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1}_1 \\
   637	    \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5} = \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5}_0 - \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5}_1 \\

    59	\section{Key theorem forms}
    60	
    61	Throughout, $q = 2^k$ with $k$ odd is an admissible field size, the tuple
    62	$(q,m,d)$ is admissible when moreover $d \ge 1$ and $m \mid q$, and
    63	$\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\F_q)$ denotes the $m$-variate polynomial representatives
    64	over $\F_q$ of individual degree at most $d$.  The comparison involves four
    65	theorem forms.
    66	\begin{enumerate}
    67	  \item \textbf{Source theorem form} (the polynomial-pair measurement).  There
    68	  is a function $\delta_S(\eps,m,d,q) = a(md)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$,
    69	  for universal constants $a > 1$ and $0 < b < 1$, such that for every
    70	  admissible $(q,m,d)$ and every projective strategy for the Pauli basis test
    71	  succeeding with probability at least $1-\eps$, there is a projective
    72	  measurement $\{\hat S_{g_X,g_Z}\}$ with outcomes pairs of polynomials in
    73	  $\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\F_q)$ whose evaluations are $\delta_S$-consistent, on
    74	  average over a uniform point $u \in \F_q^m$ and in both bases
    75	  $W \in \{X,Z\}$, with the corresponding points measurements
    76	  $\{\hat M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a\}$ of the strategy, together with the
    77	  symmetric counterpart of this relation.
    78	  \item \textbf{Missing instantiation obligation.}  The classical low
    79	  individual degree game with parameter tuple $(q,\, 2m+2,\, d,\, 1)$ is well
    80	  defined, and the combined point and line measurements assembled in the
    81	  analysis constitute a strategy for it of value at least
    82	  $1 - \delta_{\mathrm{combine}}$.  The game's question distribution draws
    83	  its axis and diagonal indices through an index function
    84	  $\chi_{2m+2}\colon \F_q \to \{1,\ldots,2m+2\}$ with classes of equal size
    85	  $q/(2m+2)$, so the game exists only when $2m+2$ divides $q$.
    86	  \item \textbf{Restricted form supported by the present route.}  The source
    87	  theorem form under the additional hypothesis $2m+2 \mid q$.  Among
    88	  admissible tuples this hypothesis holds exactly when $m = 1$ and
    89	  $q \ge 8$; it fails for every admissible tuple with $m \ge 2$ and for
    90	  $(q,m) = (2,1)$.
    91	  \item \textbf{Repaired import form} (recommended target).  Quantum
    92	  soundness of the directly indexed variant of the classical low individual
    93	  degree game over $\F_q^{m'}$, for every dimension $m' \ge 1$ and
    94	  admissible $q$, with no divisibility hypothesis: the question
    95	  distribution samples the axis index, and the diagonal prefix index,
    96	  uniformly from $\{1,\ldots,m'\}$ directly rather than through an index
    97	  function on $\F_q$, and line questions carry the sampled index itself in
    98	  place of the seed $s \in \F_q$; the error is
    99	  $\delta_{\mathrm{ld}}(\eps,q,m',d,k) = a(dm'k)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} +
   100	  2^{-bm'd})$.  This is a candidate target form, not an established one:
   101	  proving it carries the same two import obligations as the $\chi$-based
   102	  import (Section~\ref{sec:import-obligations}), and deriving the present
   103	  form from it when $m' \mid q$ requires the strategy transport described
   104	  under the candidate repairs below, whose synchronicity step is an open
   105	  obligation.
   106	\end{enumerate}

   108	\section{The source assertion and the obstruction}
   109	
   110	We examine the final step of the subsection ``Applying the classical
   111	low-degree test'' in the analysis of the Pauli basis test in the compression
   112	paper of Ji, Natarajan, Vidick, Wright, and Yuen (MIP$^{*}$=RE,
   113	arXiv:2001.04383), whose quantum soundness component builds on the low
   114	individual degree test of \cite{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree}.%
   115	\footnote{Tracked in \localissue{0002}.  In the mirror of the source
   116	consulted here, the polynomial-pair lemma and its proof are at
   117	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex},
   118	lines~1267--1288; the sub-line lemma is at lines~1063--1116 and the combined
   119	line lemma at lines~1020--1034 of the same file.  The game parametrization
   120	with its divisibility, the index function, the soundness statement with its
   121	proof, and admissibility are at
   122	\path{references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex},
   123	lines~33--35, 214--219, 413--458, and 958--961.}
   124	There, the combined point measurements
   125	$\{\hat Q^{x,z,\alpha,\beta}_c\}$ and combined line measurements
   126	$\{\hat Q^{\ell}_f\}$, indexed by points of $\F_q^{2m+2}$ and lines in
   127	$\F_q^{2m+2}$, are asserted to form a strategy for the classical low
   128	individual degree game with parameters
   129	\[
   130	  \mathsf{ldparams} = (q,\, 2m+2,\, d,\, 1)
   131	  \tag{\path{lem:qld-4-7}}
   132	\]
   133	of value $1 - \delta_{\mathrm{combine}}$, and the quantum soundness theorem
   134	for that game is applied to produce the global polynomial-pair measurement.
   135	The two lemmas feeding this step are stated for the line-point distribution
   136	over $\F_q^{2m+2}$.
   137	
   138	The game, however, is parametrized by tuples $(q,m',d,k)$ with $q$ an
   139	admissible field size \emph{and $m'$ dividing $q$}.  The divisibility is not
   140	incidental: the question distribution is a conditionally linear distribution
   141	in which a uniform seed coordinate $s \in \F_q$, read as an integer in
   142	$\{0,\ldots,q-1\}$, determines the axis or diagonal index through the unique
   143	$\chi(s)$ with
   144	\[
   145	  s = (\chi(s)-1)\,\frac{q}{m'} + r, \qquad 0 \le r < \frac{q}{m'},
   146	  \tag{\path{eq:chi-func}}
   147	\]
   148	so that the $m'$ classes $\chi^{-1}(i)$ partition $\F_q$ into sets of equal
   149	size $q/m'$ and the index is uniform.  For $m' \nmid q$ neither the index
   150	function nor the line-point distribution built from it is defined.
   151	
   152	Admissibility of $(q,m,d)$ supplies only $m \mid q$.  Since an admissible $q$
   153	is a power of two, $m \mid q$ forces $m = 2^j$.  For $j \ge 1$ the integer
   154	$m+1 \ge 3$ is odd, so $2m+2 = 2(m+1)$ has an odd factor exceeding $1$ and
   155	divides no power of two; for $m = 1$ the condition $4 \mid q$ holds for every
   156	admissible $q$ except $q = 2$.  Thus the instantiation at dimension $2m+2$ is
   157	undefined for every admissible tuple with $m \ge 2$: for instance
   158	$(q,m,d) = (8,2,1)$ is admissible, while $6 \nmid 8$.  The source performs
   159	the instantiation without addressing the divisibility, so its proof route
   160	establishes the polynomial-pair lemma, and with it the soundness theorem for
   161	the Pauli basis test that rests on it, only for $m = 1$ and $q \ge 8$.

   163	\section{What the cited soundness theorem requires: the import obligations}
   164	\label{sec:import-obligations}
   165	
   166	The quantum soundness theorem for the classical game inherits the constraint
   167	$m' \mid q$ solely because it is stated for the game just described; its
   168	proof fixes an admissible $q$ with $m' \mid q$, asserts that the game with
   169	simultaneity parameter $1$ is \emph{identical} to the two-prover tensor-code
   170	test for the Reed--Solomon tensor code $\mathcal C^{\ot m'}$ of the same
   171	authors' \emph{Quantum soundness of testing tensor codes} (arXiv:2111.08131)
   172	\cite{Ji2021Quantum}, and concludes by Theorem~4.7 there, instantiated with
   173	that theorem's auxiliary integer parameter --- denoted $k$ in that source,
   174	and written $K$ here to avoid clashing with the field exponent and the
   175	simultaneity parameter --- chosen as $(m')^3 d$.  Neither
   176	the asserted identity nor the instantiation is complete as stated, so the
   177	import carries two verification obligations, which this section details and
   178	which the blueprint's proof node for the soundness statement records as
   179	open.  Both obligations are independent of the divisibility question: they
   180	arise at every dimension, for the $\chi$-based game where it is defined and
   181	equally for the directly indexed variant proposed under the candidate
   182	repairs.
   183	
   184	\paragraph{The cited test.}
   185	In the two-prover tensor-code test (Figures~1 and~2 of
   186	\cite{Ji2021Quantum}; the two-prover strategy format and the goodness
   187	measure are Definitions~4.5 and~4.6 there), the referee performs one of
   188	three subtests with probability $1/3$ each, assigning the two roles of each
   189	subtest to the two provers uniformly at random.  \emph{Axis-parallel lines
   190	test}: sample a uniform point $u \in [n]^{m'}$ and a uniform axis
   191	$j \in \{1,\ldots,m'\}$; send the axis-parallel line $\ell$ through $u$ in
   192	direction $j$ to one prover, who answers a codeword $g \in \mathcal C$;
   193	send $u$ to the other, who answers a field value $a$; accept iff
   194	$g(u_j) = a$.  \emph{Subcube commutation test}: sample
   195	$j \in \{1,\ldots,m'\}$ and a subcube $H \subseteq [n]^{m'}$ by fixing the
   196	last $j-1$ coordinates uniformly; sample $u, v$ independently and uniformly
   197	in $H$ and a uniform order bit; send the ordered pair $(u,v)$ or $(v,u)$ to
   198	one prover, who answers a pair $(b_u, b_v)$ of field values; send $u$ to
   199	the other, who answers $a$; accept iff $b_u = a$.  \emph{Synchronicity
   200	test}: send one identical question --- a line, a point, or an ordered
   201	pair, with probability $1/3$ each --- to both provers and accept iff their
   202	answers agree.  Theorem~4.7 supposes a two-prover strategy passing this
   203	test with probability $1-\eps$ together with an integer parameter
   204	$K \ge 12 m' t$, where $t$ is the interpolation parameter of the base code
   205	--- for the degree-$d$ Reed--Solomon code, of blocklength $n = q$ and
   206	distance $q-d$, one has $t = d+1$ --- and produces projective measurements
   207	$\{G_c\}$ and $\{\tilde G_c\}$ with outcomes in $\mathcal C^{\ot m'}$,
   208	consistent with one prover's points measurements, with the other prover's
   209	lines measurements, and with each other, up to
   210	$\eta'(m',t,K,\eps,n^{-1}) = \mathrm{poly}(m',t,K) \cdot
   211	\mathrm{poly}(\eps, n^{-1}, e^{-K/(m')^2})$.
   212	
   213	\paragraph{Obligation 1: the game correspondence.}
   214	The source asserts that the $\chi$-based game at parameters $(q,m',d,1)$
   215	is this test.  It is not, in four respects.
   216	(i)~The game has no pair questions.  A pair question of the test reveals
   217	two points of a \emph{hidden} subcube --- the subcube itself is not sent
   218	--- and is answered by two field values, while the game's diagonal-line
   219	question reveals a full line description and is answered by a degree-$m'd$
   220	polynomial.  A reduction must construct the pair measurements from the
   221	diagonal-line measurements by post-processing (measure a line through $u$
   222	and $v$ and evaluate the answered polynomial at the two parameters), and
   223	both directions of the information mismatch matter: the game's line
   224	description carries an index and a seed, neither of which is a function of
   225	the pair $(u,v)$, so the constructed measurement must average over the
   226	compatible indices and seeds; and the game's diagonal lines fix the
   227	\emph{first} $i-1$ coordinates where the test's subcubes fix the
   228	\emph{last} $j-1$, so the coordinate conventions must be aligned.  The
   229	construction must preserve projectivity and must match the law of the
   230	hidden-subcube pair with the law induced by the game's diagonal sampling.
   231	(ii)~The game's line questions carry the seed $s \in \F_q$; the test's
   232	carry only the line.  A strategy may depend on the seed beyond its class
   233	$\chi^{-1}(i)$, and removing this dependence runs into the fiber-averaging
   234	difficulty made explicit under the candidate repairs: averaging preserves
   235	the line-versus-point branches exactly but not the synchronicity branches.
   236	(iii)~The branch weights differ: each nontrivial cross-test has mass $1/3$
   237	in the test against $2/9$ in the game.  Once the per-branch predicates are
   238	matched, the intended bookkeeping bound is that the constructed strategy's
   239	rejection probability in the test is at most $\tfrac32$ times the game's
   240	rejection probability, up to the $O(1/(m'q))$ of item~(iv); this bound is
   241	the target of the obligation, not an established fact.
   242	(iv)~The game's predicate fixes an acceptance convention on diagonal
   243	questions with zero direction --- an event of probability at most
   244	$2/(m'q)$, recorded in the blueprint's remark on zero directions --- for
   245	which the test has no counterpart branch.
   246	Finally, the displayed conclusions of Theorem~4.7 pair one prover's points
   247	measurements with the other prover's tensor-codeword measurement, and the
   248	first prover's tensor-codeword measurement with the second prover's lines
   249	measurements, while the game-level statement asserts the point consistency
   250	in both directions; deriving the stated form uses the role symmetrization
   251	of the test and belongs to the correspondence.  None of these steps is
   252	difficult to state, but none is carried out in the source, and together
   253	they replace the asserted one-line identity by a reduction carrying its
   254	own value bound.
   255

   260	holds at $m' = 4$ exactly when $d \ge 3$, and fails for every $d$ when

   394	We define a special class of measurements that are relevant to the soundness
   395	properties of the low-degree test.
   396	
   397	\begin{definition}[Low-degree polynomial measurements]
   398	  \label{def:ld-meas}
   399	  Define $\polymeas{m}{d}{q}$ to be the set of POVM measurements whose outcomes
   400	  correspond to (individual) degree-$d$ polynomials of $m$ variables over
   401	  $\F_q$.
   402	  More generally, for an integer $\ldc$ and tuples $m=(m_1, m_2, \ldots,
   403	  m_\ldc)$, $d=(d_1, d_2, \ldots, d_\ldc)$ and $q=(q_1, q_2, \ldots, q_\ldc)$,
   404	  we let $\simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ldc}$ be the set of measurements $G =
   405	  \{G_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots\,,\, g_\ldc}\}$ such that for $i\in\{1, 2, \ldots,
   406	  \ldc\}$, $g_i$ is a polynomial $g_i:\F_{q_i}^{m_i} \rightarrow
   407	  \F_{q_i}$ with individual degree $d_i$ (see \Cref{sec:ld-encoding} for a definition of individual degree). 
   408	\end{definition}
   409	
   410	Quantum soundness of a version of the classical low-degree test for polynomials of low \emph{total} degree was claimed
   411	in~\cite{natarajan2018low}, building on an analysis of a three-prover version of the test in~\cite{vidick2016three}. Unfortunately there is a gap in the soundness analysis of this test. For our construction we use the low individual degree test, whose quantum soundness is shown in~\cite{ML20} and generalized in~\cite{ji2021quantum}. We state the result in the form that is most directly useful for us, and show how the stated result follows from~\cite{ji2021quantum}.
   412	
   413	\begin{theorem}[Quantum soundness of the simultaneous classical low-degree test]
   414	  \label{lem:ld-soundness}
   415	  There exists a function $\delta_{\ld}(\eps, q, m, d, \ldc) = a (dm \ldc)^a (\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$ for universal constants $a\geq 1$ and $0<b\leq 1$ 
   416	such that the following
   417	  holds.
   418	  For all $\eps > 0$ and parameter tuple $\ldparams = (q, m, d, \ldc)$, for all
   419	  projective strategies $(\psi,A,B)$ that succeed with probability at least
   420	  $1-\eps$ in the game $\game^\ld_\ldparams$, there exists measurements
   421	  \[G^w \in \simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ldc}\] on $\mH_w$, for
   422	  $w\in\{\alice,\bob\}$, such that
   423	  \begin{equation*}
   424	    \begin{split}
   425	      A^{\Point,\, u}_{a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots\,,\, a_\ldc}
   426	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   427	      G^\bob_{[(g_1(u),g_2(u),\ldots,g_\ldc(u)) = (a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots \,,\, a_\ldc)]}\;,\\
   428	      G^\alice_{[(g_1(u),g_2(u),\ldots,g_\ldc(u)) = (a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots \,,\, a_\ldc)]}
   429	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   430				 B^{\Point,\, u}_{a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots\,,\, a_\ldc}\;,\\
   431	      G^\alice_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots \,,\, g_\ldc}
   432	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   433	      G^\bob_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots \,,\, g_\ldc}\;,
   434	    \end{split}
   435	  \end{equation*}
   436	  where $\delta_{\ld} = \delta_{\ld}(\eps, q, m, d, \ldc)$, 
   437	  and all three statements are with respect to the state $\ket{\psi}$.
   438	In addition, the first two approximations hold under the uniform distribution over $u\in \F_q^m$,
   439		whereas there is no question distribution associated with the third approximation.
   440	\end{theorem}
   441	
   442	\begin{proof}
   443	Let $\ldparams = (q, m, d, \ldc)$
   444	where $m, d, \ldc \in \N$ are integers, $q \in \N$ is an admissible field size,
   445	and $m$ divides $q$. Let $\Sigma=\F_q$. Let $\code \subseteq \Sigma^q$ be the Reed-Solomon code with degree $d$. Explicitly, $\code$ is the set of all $(p(x_1),\ldots,p(x_n))$ where $p:\F_q\to\F_q$ is a univariate polynomial of degree at most $d$ and $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ are an enumeration of $\F_q$. Then in the (standard) notation from~\cite{ji2021quantum} $\code$ is a linear $[q,d+1,n-d+1]_\Sigma$ code.
   446	
   447	Observe that the two-prover tensor code test, for the code $\code^{\otimes m}$, as described in~\cite[Figure 1 and Figure 2]{ji2021quantum}, is identical to the game $\game^\ld$ with parameters $\ldparams$ and $\ldc=1$, whose decider is presented in Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider}. This is because 
   448	\begin{enumerate}
   449	\item The \emph{axis-parallel line-versus-point test} from Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} is identical to the \emph{axis-parallel lines test} from~\cite[Figure 1]{ji2021quantum}, with the only difference that in Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} the roles of A and B are chosen uniformly at random. This is consistent with the two-prover variant of the tensor code test from~\cite[Section 4.1]{ji2021quantum}.
   450	\item The \emph{diagonal line-versus-point test} from Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} is identical to the \emph{subcube commutation test} from~\cite[Figure 1]{ji2021quantum}, with again the added symmetrization between players. 
   451	\item The \emph{consistency test} from Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} is identical to the \emph{synchronicity test} from~\cite[Figure 2]{ji2021quantum}.
   452	\end{enumerate}
   453	
   454	As a result,~\cite[Theorem 4.7]{ji2021quantum}, in which we choose the parameter $k$ as $k=m^3d$,  immediately yields \Cref{lem:ld-soundness}.
   455	
   456	To conclude it remains to extend the result to the case of general $\ldc$. This is done 
   457	via a standard reduction, following exactly the same steps as the derivation of Theorem 4.43 from Theorem 4.40 in~\cite{NW19}.
   458	\end{proof}

   140	Throughout the paper we abbreviate ``conditionally linear functions'' and
   141	``conditionally linear distributions'' as \emph{CL functions} and \emph{CL
   142	  distributions}, respectively.
   143	
   144	The following lemma elucidates structural properties of $\ell$-level CL
   145	functions.
   146	Recall that using our shorthand notation, $x^{L_{<k}}$ and $x^{L_k}$ in the
   147	lemma denote $L_{<k}(x)$ and $L_{k,u}(x^{V_{k,\, u}})$ where $u = L_{<k}(x)$.
   148	
   149	
   150	\begin{lemma}
   151	  \label{lem:cl-kth}
   152		Let $\ell \geq 1$ and $V = \F^n$ for some integer $n \geq 0$.
   153	  A function $L: V \to V$ is an $\ell$-level CL function if and only if the
   154	  following collection of functions and subspaces exists:
   155	  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
   156	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-marginal} For each $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$, a
   157	    function $L_{\le k} : V \to V$ called the \emph{$k$-th marginal of $L$};
   158	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-space} For each $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$ and $u
   159	    \in L_{<k} (V)$, a register subspace $V_{k,\, u}$ of $V$ called the
   160	    \emph{$k$-th factor space with prefix $u$};
   161	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-map} For each $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$ and $u \in
   162	    L_{<k} (V)$, a linear map $L_{k,\, u} : V_{k,\, u} \to V_{k,\, u}$ called
   163	    the \emph{$k$-th linear map of $L$ with prefix $u$};
   164	  \end{enumerate}
   165	  such that the following conditions hold for all $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots,
   166	  \ell\}$.
   167	  \begin{enumerate}
   168	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-cl} $L_{\leq k}$ is a $k$-level CL function on $V$;
   169		\item \label{enu:cl-space-sum} $V = \bigoplus_{i = 1}^\ell V_{i,\,
   170	      x^{L_{<i}}}$ for all $x \in V$;
   171	\item \label{enu:cl-map-sum} $L_{\leq k}(x) = \sum_{i = 1}^{k} x^{L_i}$ for
   172	    all $x \in V$, where $L_i$ is shorthand notation for $L_{i,\,
   173	      x^{L_{<i}}}$;
   174	  \item \label{enu:cl-last-ell} $L = L_{\leq \ell}$.
   175	  \end{enumerate}
   176	  As in \cref{enu:cl-map-sum}, we sometimes use $V_k$ and $L_k$ to denote
   177	  $V_{k,\, u}$ and $L_{k,\, u}$ respectively, leaving the prefix $u$ implicit.
   178	\end{lemma}
   179	
   180	\begin{proof}
   181		We first prove the ``if'' direction: if there exist spaces and functions
   182	  satisfying the conditions in the lemma, the fact that $L$ is an $\ell$-level
   183	  CL function follows from \cref{enu:cl-k-cl,enu:cl-last-ell} of the lemma
   184	  statement.
   185	
   186	  We now prove the ``only if'' direction.
   187	  Given a CL function $L$ on $V$, we construct the $k$-th family of subspaces
   188	  and functions for all $k \in \{1, \ldots, \ell\}$ by induction on the level
   189	  $\ell$.
   190	  First consider the base case $\ell=1$.
   191	  Since $L_{<1} = 0$, we omit the mentioning of the prefix $u \in L_{<1}(V)$.
   192	  Define $L_{\leq 1} = L$, the factor space $V_1 = V$, and the linear map $L_1 =
   193	  L$.
   194	  It is straightforward to verify that the conditions in the lemma hold for
   195	  these choices of linear maps and spaces.
   196	  
   197	  Now, assume that the lemma holds for CL functions of level at most $\ell - 1$,
   198	  and we prove the lemma for $\ell$-level CL functions.
   199	  By definition, an $\ell$-level CL function $L$ can be written as
   200	  \begin{equation*}
   201	  	L(x) = x^{L_1} + L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{V_{>1}})
   202	  \end{equation*}
   203	  for some linear map $L_1 : V_1 \to V_1$ and a family of $(\ell-1)$-level CL
   204	  functions
   205	  \begin{equation*}
   206	    \bigl \{ L_{>1,\, v} : V_{>1} \to V_{>1} \bigr \}_{\, v \in L_1(V_1)}
   207	  \end{equation*}
   208	  where $V_1$ and $V_{>1}$ are complementary register subspaces of $V$.
   209	  Next, using the inductive hypothesis on the $(\ell-1)$-level CL function
   210	  $L_{>1,\, v}$ we get that for all $v \in L_1(V_1)$ and all $k \in \{1, 2,
   211	  \ldots, \ell-1\}$ there exist $k$-th marginal functions $L'_{v,\, \le k}:
   212	  V_{>1} \to V_{>1}$, $k$-th factor spaces $V'_{v,\, k,\, u}$, and $k$-th linear
   213	  maps $L'_{v,\, k,\, u}$ of $L_{>1,\, v}$ with prefix $u \in L'_{v,\,
   214	    <k}(V_{>1})$ such that the conditions of the lemma for $L_{>1,\, v}$ hold.
   215	  
   216	  Define the marginal functions $L_{\le k} : V \to V$, factor spaces
   217	  $V_{k,\, u}$ and linear maps $L_{k,\, u}$ for $L$ as follows.
   218	  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
   219	  \item Define $L_{\le 1} = L_1$ and the first factor space to be $V_1$;
   220	  \item For all $k \in \{2, 3, \ldots, \ell\}$, define
   221	    \begin{equation}
   222	      \label{eq:cl-k-def}
   223	      L_{\le k}: x \mapsto x^{L_1} + L'_{x^{L_1},\, <k} (x^{V_{>1}})
   224	      \quad\text{for } x\in V;
   225	    \end{equation}
   226		\item For all $k \in \{2, 3, \ldots, \ell\}$ and $u \in L_{< k}(V)$, define
   227	    $V_{k,\, u} = V'_{v,\, k-1,\, w}$ and $L_{k,\, u} = L'_{v,\, k-1,\, w}$
   228	    where $v = u^{V_1} \in L_{1}(V_{1})$ and $w = u^{V_{>1}} \in L'_{v,< k-1}(V_{> 1})$.
   229	  \end{enumerate}
   230	  We verify that the conditions of the lemma are satisfied.
   231	  Since $L'_{v,\, < k}$ is by assumption a $(k-1)$-level CL function on $V_{>
   232	    1}$, we get that $L_{\leq k}$ is a $k$-level CL function on $V$ from
   233	  \cref{eq:cl-k-def}, establishing \cref{enu:cl-k-cl}.
   234	  By the induction hypothesis, we have for all $v\in L_1(V_1)$ and $y \in
   235	  V_{>1}$,
   236	  \begin{equation}
   237	    \label{eq:cl-k-1}
   238	    V_{>1} = \bigoplus_{i=1}^{\ell-1}
   239	    V'_{\smash{v,\, i, \, y^{L'_{v,\, <i}}}},
   240	  \end{equation}
   241	  which implies that for all $x \in V$ and $v = x^{L_1}$,
   242	  \begin{equation*}
   243	    V = V_1 \oplus \Big ( \bigoplus_{i=1}^{\ell-1}
   244	    V'_{\smash{v,\, i, \, x^{L'_{v,\, <i}}}} \Big)
   245	    = V_1 \oplus \Big (\bigoplus_{i=2}^{\ell} V_{i,\, x^{L_{<i}}} \Big)
   246	    = \bigoplus_{i=1}^\ell V_{i,\, x^{L_{<i}}}\;.
   247	  \end{equation*}
   248	  The first equality follows from \cref{eq:cl-k-1} while the second and third
   249	  equalities follow from the definition of $V_{k,\, u}$.
   250	  This establishes \cref{enu:cl-space-sum}.
   251	
   252	  Next, we have that for all $x \in V$, $v = x^{L_1}$, and $k \in
   253	  \{1,2,\ldots,\ell\}$,
   254	  \begin{align}
   255	    \label{eq:cl-last-ell}
   256	    L_{\leq k}(x)
   257	    & = v + L'_{v,\, <k} (x^{V_{>1}}) \\
   258	    & = v + \sum_{i=1}^{k-1} x^{L'_{v,\, i}}
   259	    = \sum_{i = 1}^{k} x^{L_{i}}, \label{eq:cl-last-ell2}
   260	  \end{align}
   261	  where $L'_{v,\, i}$ is the $i$-th linear map of $L_{>1,\, v}$ with prefix
   262	  $L'_{v,\, <i}(x)$ and $L_i$ is the $i$-th linear map of $L$ with prefix
   263	  $L_{<i}(x)$.
   264	  The second equality follows from the inductive hypothesis applied to $L'_{v,\,
   265	    <k}$ and the third equality follows from the definition of $L_{i}$.
   266	  Line~\eqref{eq:cl-last-ell2} implies \cref{enu:cl-map-sum} of the lemma.
   267	  
   268	  Finally, \Cref{enu:cl-last-ell} follows from~\eqref{eq:cl-last-ell} where we
   269	  set $k = \ell$ and observe that $L'_{x^{L_1},\, \le \ell-1}$ is equal to
   270	  $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ by the inductive hypothesis.
   271	  This shows that $L_{\le k}$, $V_{k,\, u}$, and $L_{k,\, u}$ satisfy the
   272	  conditions of the lemma and completes the induction.
   273	\end{proof}
   274	
   275	We note that the marginal functions, factor spaces, and linear maps of a given
   276	CL function $L$ may not be unique; for example, consider the identity function
   277	on a linear space $V = \F^n$.
   278	This is clearly a $1$-level CL function, but it can also be viewed as a
   279	$k$-level CL function for $k \in \{2, \ldots, n\}$ with an arbitrary partition
   280	of $V$ into factor spaces.
   281	
   282	\begin{lemma}
   283	  \label{lem:cl-concat}
   284	  Let $\ell, k \ge 0$ be integers and $U = \F^n$, $V = \F^m$ be linear spaces.
   285	  Suppose $L$ is a $k$-level CL function on $U$ and $R_u$ is an $\ell$-level CL
   286	  function on $V$ for each $u \in L(U)$.
   287	  Then the \emph{concatenation} $T$ of $L$ and $\{R_u\}_u$ defined as
   288	  \begin{equation*}
   289	    T (x) = L(x^U) + R_{L(x^U)} (x^V)
   290	  \end{equation*}
   291	  is a $(k+\ell)$-level conditionally linear function on $U\oplus V$.
   292	\end{lemma}
   293	
   294	\begin{proof}
   295	  We prove the claim by induction on $k$.
   296	  The case $k = 0$ follows from the Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}.
   297	  Assume that the lemma holds for $L$ being at most $(k-1)$-level.
   298	  By Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}, there are complementary register subspaces
   299	  $U_1$ and $U_{>1}$ of $U$, a linear function $L_1$ on $U_1$, and a family of
   300	  $(k-1)$-level CL functions $L_{>1,\, v}$ for $v \in L_1(U_1)$ such that
   301	  \begin{equation*}
   302	    L(x^U) = x^{L_1} + L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1}}).
   303	  \end{equation*}
   304	  For all $x^{L_1}$, define the function $T_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ on $U_{>1} \oplus V$ as
   305	  \begin{equation*}
   306	    T_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1} \oplus V}) = L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1}}) +
   307	    R_{x^{L_1} + x^{L_{>1}}}(x^V),
   308	  \end{equation*}
   309	  the concatenation of $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ and $\{ R_{L(x^U)} \}_{x^{L_{>1}}}$
   310	  where $L_{>1}$ is the shorthand notation of $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$.
   311	  By the induction hypothesis, $T_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ is $(k+\ell-1)$-level
   312	  conditionally linear.
   313	  The lemma follows from Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}.
   314	\end{proof}
   315	\begin{lemma}[Direct sums of CL functions]
   316	  \label{lem:cl-func-prod}
   317	  Let $V^{(1)}, V^{(2)}, \ldots, V^{(m)}$ be register subspaces of $V$ such that
   318	  $V = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}$.
   319	  Suppose that, for each $j\in\{1, 2, \ldots, m\}$, $L^{(j)}$ is an
   320	  $\ell_j$-level conditionally linear function on $V^{(j)}$.
   321	  Then the direct sum $L = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}$ is an $\ell$-level CL
   322	  function over $V$ for $\ell = \max_j \{\ell_j\}$, where $L$ is defined by
   323	  \begin{equation*}
   324	    L(x) = \sum_{j=1}^m  L^{(j)}(x^{(j)})
   325	  \end{equation*}
   326	  for all $x = \sum_{j=1}^m x^{(j)} \in \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}$.
   327	\end{lemma}
   328	
   329	\begin{proof}
   330	  It is easy to see that an $\ell$-level CL function is also $k$-level
   331	  conditionally linear for all $k \ge \ell$.
   332	  Hence, it suffices to prove the claim where $\ell_j = \ell$ for $j=1, 2,
   333	  \ldots, m$.
   334	
   335	  We prove the theorem by an induction on $\ell$.
   336	  For $\ell = 1$, the functions $L^{(j)}$ are linear and the claim follows by
   337	  the fact that the direct sum of linear maps is linear.
   338	
   339	  Assume now the theorem holds for conditionally linear functions of level at
   340	  most $\ell-1$ and $L^{(j)}$ are $\ell$-level conditionally linear functions
   341	  for $j=1, 2, ,\ldots, m$.
   342	  By definition, $L^{(j)}$ is the concatenation of conditionally linear
   343	  functions $L^{(j)}_{1}$ on $V^{(j)}_1$ and $\{ L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j} \}_{v_j}$
   344	  on $V^{(j)}_{>1}$ of levels $1$, and $\ell-1$ respectively.
   345	  Furthermore,
   346	  \begin{equation*}
   347	    L(x) = \sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)} (x^{(j)}) = \sum_{j=1}^m \Bigl( v_j +
   348	    L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j}
   349	    \Bigl((x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_{>1}} \Bigr) \Bigr),
   350	  \end{equation*}
   351	  where $v_j = L^{(j)}_{1}\Bigl( (x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_1}
   352	    \Bigr)$.
   353	  By the induction hypothesis,
   354	  \begin{equation*}
   355	    L_{1} (x^{V_1}) = \sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}_{1}\Bigl( (x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_1}
   356	    \Bigr),\quad L_{>1,\, v} (x^{V_{>1}}) = \sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j}
   357	    \Bigl((x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_{>1}} \Bigr)
   358	  \end{equation*}
   359	  are $1$-level and $(\ell-1)$-level conditionally linear respectively for $v =
   360	  \sum_j v_j$, $V_1 = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}_1$, and $V_{>1} =
   361	  \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}_{>1}$.
   362	  This proves that $L$ is $\ell$-level conditionally linear.
   363	\end{proof}
   364	
   365	\begin{lemma}
   366	  \label{lem:cl-dist-prod}
   367	  For each $i \in \{1,\ldots,m\}$ let $L^{(i)}, R^{(i)} : V^{(i)} \to V^{(i)}$
   368	  be $\ell_i$-level conditionally linear functions and let $L, R: V \to V$ be the
   369	  direct sums $L = \bigoplus_i L_i$ and $R = \bigoplus_i R_i$, respectively, as
   370	  defined in Lemma~\ref{lem:cl-func-prod}.
   371	  Then the conditionally linear distribution $\mu_{L, R}$ is the product
   372	  distribution $\prod_{i=1}^m \mu_{L^{(i)},\, R^{(i)}}$ over $V \times V$.
   373	\end{lemma}

   375	\begin{proof}
   376		The distribution $\mu_{L,R}$ is the distribution over pairs $(L(x),R(x))$
   377	  where $x$ is sampled uniformly from $V \times V$.

   379	  pairs $\bigl( (L_i(x^{V_i}))_{i=1}^m, (R_i(x^{V_i}))_{i=1}^m \bigr)$ where $x$
   380	  is chosen uniformly at random from $V$.
   381	  This distribution is exactly the product of the distributions $
   382	  \mu_{L^{(i)},\, R^{(i)}}$ for $i = 1, 2, \ldots, m$.
   383	\end{proof}
