    62	  exact Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨(0, 0), Finset.mem_univ _, rfl⟩

    79

    81	finite-carrier infrastructure for `def:ms-game`, blueprint
    82	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
    83	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.

    89	  invFun
    90	    | .inl β => .triple β
    91	    | .inr γ => .bit γ

    93	  right_inv := by

219	\begin{definition}[Distance between states]
   220	  \label{def:state-distance}
   221	
   222		Let $\{\ket{\psi_n}\}_{n\in \N}$ and $\{\ket{\psi'_n}\}_{n\in \N}$ be two
   223	  families of states in the same space $\mH$.
   224	  For some function $\delta : \N \to [0,1]$ we say that $\{ \ket{\psi_n} \}$ and
   225	  $\{ \ket{\psi'_n} \}$ are \emph{$\delta$-close}, denoted as $\ket{\psi}
   226	  \approx_\delta \ket{\psi'}$, if $ \norm{\ket{\psi_n} - \ket{\psi'_n}}^2 =
   227	  O(\delta(n))$.
   228	  (For convenience we generally leave the dependence of the states and $\delta$
   229	  on the indexing parameter $n$ implicit, writing e.g.\ $\ket{\psi}$ for $\ket{\psi_n}$.)
   230	\end{definition}
   231	
   232	\begin{definition}[Consistency between POVMs]
   233	  \label{def:consistency}
   234		Let $\mX$ be a finite set and $\mu$ a distribution on $\mX$.
   235	  Let $\ket{\psi} \in \cal{H}_A \otimes \cal{H}_B$ be a quantum state, and for
   236	  all $x\in \mX$, $\{A^x_a\}$ and $\{B^x_a\}$ POVMs.
   237	  We write
   238	  \begin{equation*}
   239	    A^x_a \otimes I_\bob \simeq_\delta I_\alice \otimes B^x_a
   240	  \end{equation*}
   241	  on state $\ket{\psi}$ and distribution $\mu$ if
   242	  \begin{equation*}
   243	    \E_{x\sim \mu} \sum_{a\ne b} \bra{\psi} A^x_a \otimes B^x_b \ket{\psi}
   244	    = O(\delta)\;.\footnote{Here the use of the $O(\cdot)$ notation refers to the fact that the notation will often be used to measure consistency for \emph{famillies} of POVM and states indexed by an implicit parameter $n\in \mathbb{N}$, which will always be clear from context but omitted for legibility, see Definition~\ref{def:state-distance}. The $O(\cdot)$ is taken as $n\to\infty$.}
   245	  \end{equation*}
   246	  In this case, we say that $\{A^x_a\}$ and $\{B^x_a\}$ are
   247	  \emph{$\delta$-consistent} on $\ket{\psi}$.
   248	\end{definition}
   249	
   250	Note that a consistent measurement on $\ket{\psi}$ according to
   251	Definition~\ref{def:consistent-measurement} is $0$-consistent with itself on the same $\ket{\psi}$ and under
   252	the singleton distribution, according to Definition~\ref{def:consistency} (and
   253	vice-versa). This is because 
   254	\[ \sum_a \bra{\psi} M_a \otimes M_a \ket{\psi} =1 \,\implies \, \forall a\;,\;\Id\otimes M_a \ket{\psi} = M_a \otimes \Id \ket{\psi}\;,\]
   255	because using that $\{M_a\}$ is a POVM there must be equality in the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality
   256	\[ 1 = \sum_a \bra{\psi} M_a \otimes M_a \ket{\psi}\, \leq\, \Big(\sum_a \|\Id\otimes M_a \ket{\psi}\|^2 \Big)\Big(\sum_a \|M_a\otimes \Id \ket{\psi}\|^2 \Big)^{1/2} \,\leq\,1 \;.\]
   257	
   258	\begin{definition}[Distance between POVMs]
   259	  \label{def:povm-distance}
   260		Let $\mX$ be a finite set and $\mu$ a distribution on $\mX$. 
   261	  Let $\ket{\psi} \in \cal{H}$ be a quantum state, and for all $x\in \mX$,
   262	  $\{M^x_a\}$ and $\{N^x_a\}$ two POVMs on $\mH$.
   263	  We say that \emph{$\{M^x_a\}$ and $\{N^x_a\}$ are $\delta$-close on state
   264	    $\ket{\psi}$ and under distribution $\mu$} if
   265	  \begin{equation*}
   266	    \E_{x\sim \mu} \sum_a \norm{ (M^x_a - N^x_a) \ket{\psi} }^2 \leq O(\delta)\;,
   267	  \end{equation*}

   269	  $\ket{\psi}$ and distribution $\mu$ are clear from context.
   270	  This distance is referred to as the \emph{state-dependent} distance.

   273	\begin{definition}[Distance between strategies]
   274	  \label{def:strategy-distance}
   275	  Let $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{Y}, \cal{A}, \cal{B}, \mu, D)$ be a nonlocal game

   277	  strategies for $\game$.

    57	\begin{definition}[Typed conditionally linear functions]
    58	  Let $\type$ be a finite set and $V$ be $\F^n$ for some integer $n \geq 0$.
    59	  A \emph{$\type$-typed family of $\ell$-level conditionally linear functions}
    60	  (implicitly, \emph{on $V$}) is a collection $\{L_\tvar\}_{\tvar \in \type}$
    61	  such that, for each $\tvar \in \type$, $L_\tvar$ is an $\ell$-level
    62	  conditionally linear function on~$V$.
    63	\end{definition}
    64	
    65	\begin{definition}[Graph distribution]
    66	  \label{def:graph-distribution}
    67	  Let $G = (U, E)$ be an undirected graph with vertex set $U$ and edge set~$E$.
    68	  Edges in~$E$ are written as multisets $\{u, v\}$ of two vertices; the case $u
    69	  = v$ represents a self-loop.
    70	  Suppose there are $m$ edges, $k$ of which are self-loops.
    71	  Then the \emph{graph distribution $\mu_G$ of~$G$} is the distribution over
    72	  $U\times U$ such that for every $(u, v)\in U\times U$,
    73	  \begin{equation*}
    74	    \mu_G(u, v) =
    75	    \begin{cases}
    76	      1/(2m-k) & \text{if $\{u, v\} \in E$},\\
    77	      0 & \text{otherwise}.
    78	    \end{cases}
    79	  \end{equation*}
    80	  This is identical to the uniform distribution over pairs $(u, v)\in U\times U$
    81	  such that $\{u, v\} \in E$.
    82	\end{definition}
    83	
    84	\begin{definition}[Typed conditionally linear distributions]
    85	  Let $\type$ be a type set and
    86	  $L=\{L_\lvar\}_{\lvar\in\type},R=\{R_\rvar\}_{\rvar\in\type}$ be $\type$-typed
    87	  families of conditionally linear functions on~$V$.
    88	  Let $G = (\type, E)$ be a graph with vertex set $\type$.
    89	  The \emph{$(\type, G)$-typed conditionally linear distribution $\mu_{L,\,
    90	      R}^G$ corresponding to~$(L, R)$} is the distribution over pairs $( (\lvar,
    91	  x), (\rvar, y) )$, where $(\lvar, \rvar)$ is drawn from $\mu_G$ and $(x,y)$ is
    92	  drawn from $\mu_{L_\lvar,\, R_\rvar}$.
    93	\end{definition}

    96	  \label{def:typed-sampler}

132	\begin{definition}
   133	  \label{def:comm-strategy}
   134	  Let $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{Y}, \cal{A}, \cal{B}, \mu, D)$ be a game, and let
   135	  $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ be a strategy for $\game$ such that  $\mH_A = \mH_B$.
   136	  Let $S \subseteq \cal{X} \times \cal{Y}$ denote the support of the question
   137	  distribution $\mu$, i.e.\ the set of $(x,y)$ such that $\mu(x,y)>0$.
   138	  We say that $\strategy$ is a \emph{commuting strategy for $\game$} if for all
   139	  question pairs $(x, y) \in S$, we have $[A^x_a, B^y_b] = 0$ 
   140	  for all $a
   141	  \in \cal{A}, b \in \cal{B}$, where $[A, B] = AB - BA$ denotes the commutator.
   142	\end{definition}
   143	
   144	\begin{definition}[Consistent measurements]
   145	  \label{def:consistent-measurement}
   146	  Let $\cal{A}$ be a finite set, let $\ket{\psi} \in \mH \otimes \mH$ be a
   147	  state, and let $\{ M_a \}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ be a projective measurement on
   148	  $\mH$.
   149	  We say that \emph{$\{M_a\}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ is consistent on $\ket{\psi}$} if
   150	  and only if
   151	  \begin{equation*}
   152	    \forall a \in \mA\;,\quad M_a \otimes \Id_\bob\, \ket{\psi}
   153	    = \Id_\alice \otimes M_a\, \ket{\psi}\;.
   154	  \end{equation*}
   155		When the state $\ket{\psi}$ is clear from context we simply say that \emph{$\{M_a\}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ is consistent}.
   156	\end{definition}
   157	
   158	The terminology ``consistent'' arises from the fact that when the measurement $\{M_a\}$ is performed on both registers of $\ket{\psi}$, the probability of obtaining twice the same outcome is 
   159	\[ \sum_a \bra{\psi} M_a \otimes M_a \ket{\psi}\,=\, \sum_a \bra{\psi} \Id_\alice \otimes (M_a)^2 \ket{\psi} \,=\, \sum_a \bra{\psi} \Id_\alice \otimes M_a \ket{\psi} \,=\,1\;,\]
   160	where the first equality is by definition of consistency, the second uses that $\{M_a\}$ is projective, and the last uses $\sum_a M_a=\Id$. 
   161	
   162	\begin{definition}[Consistent strategies]
   163	  \label{def:consistent-strategy}
   164		Let $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ be a projective strategy with state
   165	  $\ket{\psi} \in \mH \otimes \mH$, for some Hilbert space~$\mH$, which is
   166	  defined on question alphabets $\cal{X}$ and~$\cal{Y}$ and answer alphabets
   167	  $\cal{A}$ and~$\cal{B}$, respectively.
   168	  We say that the strategy $\strategy$ is \emph{consistent} if for all $x \in
   169	  \cal{X}$, the measurement $\{A^x_a\}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ is consistent on
   170	  $\ket{\psi}$ and if for all $y \in \cal{Y}$, the measurement $\{B^y_b\}_{b \in
   171	    \cal{B}}$ is consistent on $\ket{\psi}$.
   172	\end{definition}
   173	
   174	We almost always restrict our attention to symmetric strategies. In this case, consistency implies that whenever both players are sent the same question, they provide the same answer. 
   175	
   176	\begin{definition}
   177	  \label{def:spcc}
   178	  We say that a strategy $\strategy$ for a game $\game$ is \emph{PCC} if it is projective, consistent, and commuting for $\game$.
   179	  Additionally, we say that a PCC strategy $\strategy$ is \emph{SPCC} if it is furthermore symmetric.
   180	\end{definition}

   184	\[ \ket{\psi} = \sum_{i=1}^k\, \alpha_i \ket{u_i}\otimes \ket{v_i}\;,\]

   247	  and let $\line = \line(u_0,e_i)$ where $i = \chi(s)$.

   250	  \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$.

   254	  have that $i$ is uniformly random between $\{1,2,\ldots,m\}$ and therefore
   255	  $(u_0,s)$ specifies a uniformly random axis-parallel line $\line(u_0,e_i)$.
   256	  Since $u_0 = L^{\lnf}_{e_i}(u)$, we have that $u \in \line(u_0,e_i)$.
   257	\end{proof}

   487	By definition, the trace is an $\Fq$-linear map from $\F_{q^k}$ to

   494	A \emph{dual basis} $\{e_1', e_2', \ldots, e_k' \}$ of $\{e_1, e_2, \ldots,

   497	A \emph{self-dual basis} is one that is equal to its dual.
   498	If for some $\alpha \in \F_{q^k}$ the set $\{ \alpha^{q^j} \}_{j=0}^{k-1}$ forms a
   499	basis of $\F_{q^k}$ over $\Fq$, the basis is called a \emph{normal

   242		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.IsDualBasisPair, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Basis.IsSelfDual, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Basis.IsNormal, MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_selfDualNormalBasis}

   245		A \emph{dual basis} $\{e_1', \dots, e_k'\}$ of a basis
   246		$\{e_1, \dots, e_k\}$ of $\F_{q^k}$ over $\F_q$ is a basis such that
   247		$\tr_{q^k \to q}(e^{}_i e'_j) = \delta_{i,j}$ for all
   248		$i, j \in \{1, \dots, k\}$. A \emph{self-dual basis} is one equal to its own
   249		dual. If for some $\alpha \in \F_{q^k}$ the set
   250		$\{\alpha^{q^j}\}_{j=0}^{k-1}$ forms a basis of $\F_{q^k}$ over $\F_q$, that
   251		basis is called a \emph{normal basis}. Self-dual and normal bases do not
   252		exist for every field extension, but for $q = 2$ and odd $k$ a self-dual
   253		normal basis of $\F_{2^k}$ over $\F_2$ always exists; \cite{Ji2020MIPStar}
   254		exhibits one through an explicit construction.
   255		In the formalization, a basis index in $\operatorname{Fin}(k)$ has value
   256		$j-1$ when it represents the paper's index $j\in\{1,\ldots,k\}$.
   257	\end{definition}

## Findings

- [ ] F1 (blocker) `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Games/DistributionAux.lean:121` — `Distribution.restrict_isProbability` is an untracked direct `sorry` outside the Stage 4.2 obligation inventory.
- [ ] F2 (blocker) `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Games/Consistency.lean:20` — The linked consistency and strategy-closeness predicates replace normalized bipartite asymptotic relations with unrestricted pointwise inequalities.
- [ ] F3 (blocker) `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Games/StrategyClasses.lean:104` — Measurement and strategy consistency omit the projectivity required by the source definitions.
- [ ] F4 (blocker) `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Games/StrategyClasses.lean:129` — `Strategy.IsPCC` is detached from any `Strategy G` and accepts a distribution unrelated to the game.
- [ ] F5 (blocker) `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Games/DistanceTheorems.lean:56` — The linked one-projector agreement theorem handles only the left family, not the paper’s either-family hypothesis.
- [ ] F6 (blocker) `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Games/TypedCondLinear.lean:34` — `typedCLDistribution` accepts arbitrary families without the source conditional-linearity premise.
- [ ] F7 (blocker) `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineDefs.lean:55` — Axis-line outcomes retain a seed absent from the source geometric carrier, changing the distribution’s pushforward weights.
- [ ] F8 (blocker) `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/MagicSquareTheorems.lean:105` — Magic Square rigidity compares an unnormalized `.bit` constructor slice instead of the source binary POVM.
- [ ] F9 (blocker) `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/Soundness.lean:159` — Pauli soundness compares an unnormalized `.pauliOutcome` slice instead of the source `F_q^M`-indexed POVM.
- [ ] F10 (changes) `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Algebra/SelfDualBasis.lean:34` — `Basis.IsNormal` leaves its Frobenius exponent unrelated to the base field’s cardinality.
- [ ] F11 (changes) `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Games/ErrorFunctions.lean:18` — The separate prefactor/exponent correction lacks the required `Local fix` paper-gap record and cites the wrong square-root line.
- [ ] F12 (changes) `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/MagicSquareTheorems.lean:150` — `exists_ms_rigidity` labels conventions already stated in the canonical paper as a local correction.

## Review

F1 is the only direct proof hole I found outside the tracked skeleton. `local/briefs/42-residual-brief.md:207-214` authorizes marker-free `sorry`s for its enumerated Stage 4.2 statements and companions, whereas restriction belongs to the later chapter-15 work recorded at `local/briefs/42-ch15-brief.md:151`. This theorem must be proved, removed from this PR, or explicitly added to the tracked inventory.

F2 conflicts with `def:consistency` at `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:232-248`: the source has a probability distribution, normalized bipartite state, POVMs on opposite tensor factors, and an `O(δ)` relation. Lean accepts an unnormalized `Distribution`, arbitrary same-space operators and vector, and asserts an exact `≤ δ`. `AreCloseStrategies` also omits the source bound `δ ∈ [0,1]` and its asymptotic/either-state semantics from lines 273-288. The linked blueprint explicitly preserves those semantics at `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:195-240`. Raw numerical defects may remain separately named helpers, but they cannot be the green source predicates.

For F3 and F4, paper lines 144-180 define consistency only for projective measurements and define PCC as a property of a strategy for its game. Add projectivity to the source-facing consistency predicates, and make `Strategy.IsPCC` consume the actual strategy and `G.μ`; otherwise rename the current raw-data predicates as internal auxiliaries.

F5 narrows `fact:agreement`, item 3, from “either measurement is projective” at paper lines 306-309 to left projectivity only. A faithful disjunctive theorem, or both left and right variants with a faithful wrapper, is required.

F6 omits the premise at `references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:57-63,84-93` that both inputs are typed families of conditionally linear functions. Bundle that evidence or separate the unrestricted bind construction from the source-named definition.

F7 disagrees with `def:line-point-dist` at paper lines 276-283, where an axis outcome is the geometric line `(u₀,e_i)` after `i = χ(s)`. When `χ` has nontrivial fibers, Lean records distinct outcomes for seeds representing the same line. Keep the seed in an auxiliary sampler witness and push forward to geometric lines, or state an explicit non-source distribution under a separate name.

F8 and F9 arise from global sum answer types. A `Measurement MsAnswer` can retain mass on `.triple` outcomes at a variable question, so its `.bit` slice need not sum to one; the same holds for `.pauliOutcome` among the seven `PauliAnswer` constructors. The source conclusions use genuine POVMs and explicitly sum over bits at paper lines 624-646 and over `u ∈ F_q^M` at lines 1431-1444. Use total postprocessing of malformed constructors, analogous to `ldPointValuesOrZero`. The B-side and `QubitForm.lean:119,130` inherit F9.

For F10, paper `04_preliminaries.tex:498-502` and blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:241-251` use `q = |F|` in the powers `α^(q^j)`. Use `Fintype.card F` or carry the finite-field/cardinality relation explicitly.

F11’s mathematical motivation is plausible: the paper’s coupled-constant convention is at `04_preliminaries.tex:23-29`, while the actual square-root uses occur at chapter-14 lines 508-520 and 649-676. Because this changes the stated convention, project policy requires a cited paper-gap note and `**Local fix:**` marker.

F12 should simply remove `**Local fix:**`: the QPBT paper itself states Euclidean `O(√ε)` at line 626 and explains both the norm conversion and local basis change at lines 650-652.

The full patch and prior ledger were reviewed. The repaired sandwich, pasting, symmetrization, low-degree postprocessing, and four paper-gap notes now address their earlier findings. `git diff --check` is clean, and no new axiom or prohibited proof bypass was found. Exact-head local CI was already green; I did not rerun a write-producing build in the read-only reviewer session. The external `lean-conventions` skill was unavailable, so I applied the checked-in proof-integrity and project-convention documents.
